Overview/March 1, 2027 Deadline

Deadline & Action Timeline · FY2027 Pied-à-Terre Surcharge

Missed the October 13 exemption deadline? What NYC owners can still do before March 1, 2027

Around 8,000 NYC properties saw an initial pied-à-terre surcharge appear on November 14 tax statements ahead of January 1, 2027 billing. Here is the exact timeline from October 13 to the March 1 and March 15 Tax Commission Form TC107 deadlines.

Look up your exact parcel exposure in seconds: Run your address or 10-digit BBL on our Live NYC Unit & BBL Pied-à-Terre Checker → (968,294 FY2027 DOF parcels) to verify whether your property sits in an appeal cliff zone and optionally generate a 2-page Valuation & TC107 Prep Dossier ($39).

Where the calendar stands right now

  • July 24, 2026: DOF published its supplemental surcharge roll identifying ~17,000 properties above Phase 1 whole-parcel thresholds ($1,000,000 DOF value for Class 2 condos/co-ops; $5,000,000 for Class 1 houses).
  • October 13, 2026 (Passed): Initial DOF administrative deadline to file for a primary-residence or qualifying-rental exemption. Roughly 8,900 exemptions were processed before billing.
  • November 4 & November 14, 2026: After an appellate court lifted an earlier lower-court pause on November 4, initial surcharge charges hit ~8,000 public tax statements dated November 14 ($48,609 median across the 39 billed units per 100 sampled above-cutoff $4M–$6M condos) ahead of January 1, 2027 collections.
  • March 1, 2027 (Class 2 Condos/Co-ops) & March 15, 2027 (Class 1 Houses): Statutory deadline to file paper Form TC107 with the NYC Tax Commission.

What to do before March 1 if you were billed (or missed Oct 13)

  1. Check your unit’s threshold margin and property class: Look up your parcel on api.nychousingdata.com. Condos and co-ops just above $1,000,000, $3,000,000, or $5,000,000 sit on sharp whole-parcel cliffs where reducing DOF value by even a few percent can wipe out $40,000+ per year in surcharge exposure. For co-ops, confirm how many shares your apartment holds against total building shares.
  2. Assemble primary-residence or statutory exemption proof: If the home is your primary residence, leased to a primary-residence tenant, or qualifies for a statutory exclusion, gather NYS/NYC tax filings, driver’s license/voter registration, utility bills, or lease agreements — plus entity/trust documentation if held in an LLC or trust. Under Tax Commission rules, an unchallenged missed DOF exemption requires pairing Form TC107 with a valuation challenge before the March deadline.
  3. Respect Tax Commission paper-only filing & class evidence rules: Print and sign a separate paper Form TC107 for each unit/parcel (wet signature; mail or hand-deliver to 1 Centre Street, Room 2400, New York, NY 10007 — no email or fax), and remember that Class 2 condos/co-ops are reviewed under RPTL § 581 comparable rental income rather than unit sale prices.
